outcome: Onset of motor anaesthesia (Bromage scale II)
cohort: The study included 60 parturients aged 18-30 years with ASA grades II who were scheduled for elective caesarean section.
finding: The study found that 0.5% hyperbaric bupivacaine provided a quicker onset of motor anaesthesia, while 0.75% hyperbaric ropivacaine demonstrated quicker two-segment regression, ultimately concluding ropivacaine is an acceptable substitute for bupivacaine in elective C-sections.
